SIKA® FLOORJOINT EX A: SPECIFICATION CLAUSE SET

Source: Sika® FloorJoint EX A, April 2023, Version 02.03 (https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/2/sika-floorjoint-exa.pdf)
Draft for specifier review. Wording, values and standards are quoted from that data sheet; where it is silent the clause says 'Refer to manufacturer.' Confirm the current edition before issue.

1 SCOPE
1.1 Work included. Provide Sika® FloorJoint EX A where documented, installed or applied in accordance with this clause and the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.03).
1.2 Product description. Sika® FloorJoint EX A is a prefabricated, glass-carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) composite Floor joint panel with high mechanical resistance for normal up to medium wear loading conditions. Its sinusoidal surface tooth profile allows for an improved load distribution and results in minimum vibrations, impact load and joint protection, generally for use with forklifts, pallet trucks, AGV and LGV traffic conditions.
1.3 Intended uses stated by the manufacturer.
    - Floor joint panel for new build and refurbishment of joints for concrete screeds with normal up to medium heavy wear e.g. for storage and assembly halls, maintenance workshops, hospitals, schools and ware houses.
    - Particularly used in the food and pharmaceutical industries, for show rooms, workshops and production areas etc.
    - LGV, AGV, Forklift traffic conditions to resolve ongoing concrete floor joint issues.
1.4 Limits of use. Observe the manufacturer's limitations stated in clause 4.4.

2 MATERIALS
2.1 Product. Sika® FloorJoint EX A
    - Product type as printed on the data sheet: CARBON FIBRE PREFABRICATED FLOOR JOINT PANEL FOR USE IN HIGH AND SMOOTH TRAFFIC ENVIROMENTS
    - Supplier as printed on the data sheet: Sika Australia Pty Limited, ABN 12 001 342 329, aus.sika.com, Tel: 1300 22 33 48
2.2 Approvals / certificates.
    - Reaction to fire classification acc. to DIN EN 13301-1.
    - Test report No.: KB-Hoch-140803.
    - The fire behaviour of the polymeric material of Sika® FloorJoint EX A is classified as: Bfl-s1.
2.3 Standards and test methods cited in the data sheet. Cited as written in the data sheet. A citation is not a statement that the product complies with it; conformity is stated only where the data sheet says so (see the approvals clause and the statements quoted in the other clauses).
    - DIN EN 13301-1: listed under approvals, certificates or standards. Where: Approvals / Certificates (p.1).
    - DIN EN 196-1: test method printed beside a stated value. Where: Technical Information > Compressive strength (p.2); Technical Information > Tensile strength (p.2).
2.4 Characteristics stated by the manufacturer.
    - Suitable for heavy loads
    - Rapid implementation for driving on after 24 hours
    - No unevenness, ultra-flat, 0mm Transitions possible
    - No vibration while driving
    - Allows horizontal movement
    - High chemical resistance
    - Suitable for food products
    - Temperature and weather resistance
2.5 Composition, appearance and supply.
    - Composition: PUR
    - Appearance and colour: Grey, approx.Ral7037
2.6 Properties stated by the manufacturer.
    - Dimensions: Length x width x height: approx. 1200 mm x 255 mm x 15 mm
    - Compressive strength: ~ 110 N/mm² (14days after�at 23°C / 50% R.H) DIN EN 196-1
    - Tensile strength: ~ 50 N/mm² (14days after, at 23°C / 50% R.H) DIN EN 196-1
2.7 Joint design.
    | Gap width | Maximum:55mm | Minimum:5mm |
    | Positive horizontal joint | +15mm | +65mm |
    | movement |
    | Negative horizontal | -10mm | -5mm |
    | joint movement |
    | Please contact Sika technical service for details. |
    (Table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows.)
2.8 Systems.
    | Adhesive Bed | SikaDur 31 (Approx 6kg/perLM) Sub- |
    | ject to concrete Profile |
    | Sika Floorjoint EX-A | PCE |
    | Top Coat | Sikafloor 161/264  @ 0.3kg - |
    | 0.4kg/m2 As required by site prefer-ence (Wearing Course Indicator) |
    (System build-up table as printed; a cell that wraps appears over several rows. Refer to the data sheet (page 2) for the layout.)
2.9 Consumption. 1 piece for 1.2 linear meter.
2.10 Ambient air temperature. +10°C min. / +30°C max.
2.11 Relative air humidity. 80%R.H. max
2.12 Dew point. Beware of condensation! The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3°C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish.
2.13 Substrate temperature. +10°C min. / +30°C max. The substrate and uncured floor must be at least 3°C above dew point to reduce the risk of condensation or blooming on the floor finish.
2.14 Substrate moisture content. < 4% moisture content. Test method: Sika®-Tramex meter, CM - measurement or Oven-dry-method. No rising moisture according to ASTM (Polyethylene-sheet).
2.15 Packaging, shelf life and storage.
    - Packaging: 111 pieces on an EU-pallet weight, approx. ~8.35kg/PCS
    - Shelf life: 3 years
    - Storage conditions: In cool and dry conditions at temperatures between +5°C and +30°C, always in horizontal and flat position.

3 SUBSTRATE PREPARATION
3.1 General. Prepare substrates in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.03) and the requirements below. Inspect the substrate against these requirements before application.
3.2 Substrate quality / pre-treatment. Refer to the Method Statement “Evaluation & Preparation of flooring surfaces”.

4 APPLICATION
4.1 General. Apply in accordance with the manufacturer's Product Data Sheet (April 2023, Version 02.03) and the requirements below.
4.2 Application. Please refer to the product data sheet of Sikadur®-31 CF Normal and/or the Method Statement “Sika® FloorJoint EX A”.
4.3 Cleaning of equipment. Please refer to the product data sheet of Sikadur®-31 CF Normal.
4.4 Limitations and important considerations.
    - This eccentric joint profile must be installed 85 mm offset (eccentric) from the edge of the existing joint .Please refer to Sika Drawings.
    - To avoid the risk of crack occur on the panel surface after a certain time,Cut a joint of 20mm deep and at least 5mm wide in the end of floorjoint that will isolate the effect of ground movement.
    - The Product must only be applied in accordance with its intended use, do remember indoor use only.
    - Always store Sika® FloorJoint EX A panels in horizontal position.
    - Never remove the masking tape affixed to the bottom side of the Sika® FloorJoint EX A panel. The masking tape is necessary to keep the two composite parts of the panel separate, allowing the movement of the joint after installation.
    - No relative vertical displacement of the concrete slabs can occur along the length of either side of the joint. Where necessary, apply appropriate measures such as anchoring/bolting or ground consolidation by injection prior to installation of the Sika® FloorJoint EX A panel.
    - Do not exceed the maximum positive joint movement capacity, otherwise the teeth of the panel become unsupported and may break.
    - Settlement of the substrate or of the adhesive can result in cracks in Sika® FloorJoint EX A. These cracks do not constitute a defect, since they do not affect the viability and suitability for use.
    - Do not exceed the maximum grinding depth of 2 mm. If after grinding the letters on the top surface of Sika® FloorJoint EX A are no longer visible, the maximum grinding depth of 2 mm has been exceeded and the mechanical resistance of the profile is reduced. Replace the panel if the maximum grinding depth has been exceeded.
    - The sealant may break at a positive joint movement of ~10–15 mm, however this does not affect the technical performance of Sika® FloorJoint EX A. The purpose of the joint sealant is the reduction of dirt pick-up in the joint, not to provide water tightness. Install Sikadur® Combiflex® SG System below Sika® FloorJoint EX A if a waterproof joint design is required.
    - Periodically inspect the joint sealing material and renew if necessary.
    - Do not use a hammer for placing and adjusting the floor panel during installation.

5 QUALITY CONTROL AND TESTING
5.1 Hold point. Before each application, confirm the site conditions with the manufacturer. HOLD POINT: do not proceed until the Superintendent has released the hold point.
5.2 Conditions to be verified. Refer to manufacturer. The data sheet reviewed (April 2023, Version 02.03) lists no application condition limits.
5.3 Test methods printed beside stated values. Each value is as printed in the data sheet with its test method.
    - Compressive strength: ~ 110 N/mm² (14days after�at 23°C / 50% R.H) DIN EN 196-1
    - Tensile strength: ~ 50 N/mm² (14days after, at 23°C / 50% R.H) DIN EN 196-1
5.4 Basis of the stated values. All technical data stated in this Product Data Sheet are based on laboratory tests. Actual measured data may vary due to circumstances beyond our control.
5.5 Other tests. For any test method, sampling frequency or acceptance criterion not stated in this clause: refer to manufacturer and the project specification.

6 WARRANTY AND DOCUMENTATION
6.1 Documents to be obtained and submitted. Obtain the current issue of each document before ordering and submit it with the product submission. Documents are listed as published on the manufacturer's website.
    - Product Data Sheet: Sika® FloorJoint EX A, April 2023, Version 02.03, https://aus.sika.com/content/dam/dms/au01/2/sika-floorjoint-exa.pdf
6.2 Ecology, health and safety. This product is an article as defined in article 3 of regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH). It contains no substances which are intended to be released from the article under normal or reasonably foreseeable conditions of use. A safety data sheet following article 31 of the same regulation is not needed to bring the product to the market, to transport or to use it. For safe use follow the instructions given in the product data sheet. Based on our current knowledge, this product does not contain SVHC (substances of very high concern) as listed in Annex XIV of the REACH regulation or on the candidate list published by the European Chemicals Agency in concentrations above 0,1 % (w/w).
6.3 Warranty. Obtain any product or installation warranty in writing from the manufacturer or its authorised applicator and file it with the project records. Warranty terms: refer to manufacturer.
    - Legal notes: In practice, the differences in materials, substrates and actual site conditions are such that no warranty in respect of merchantability or of fitness for a particular purpose, nor any liability arising out of any legal relationship whatsoever, can be inferred either from this information, or from any written recommendations, or from any other advice offered.
6.4 Local restrictions. Please note that as a result of specific local regulations the declared data for this product may vary from country to country. Please consult the local Product Data Sheet for the exact product data.
6.5 Application records. Record the product name, batch numbers, dates, areas treated and the conditions measured under clause 5.1, and include the records in the project documentation.
